channel.title: The SalonForge journal
channel.description: How salons actually run — booking, colour, phone, stock and pay.

item.title: From application to first shift: a hiring plan for a small salon
item.description: A stylist hire does not need a recruitment process, just six steps done in order between clients: advert, reply, call, trade test, offer, first day. What a good trade test actually looks like.

item.title: Why can't I find hairdressers? Recruiting stylists in 2026
item.description: The stylist shortage is real, not a sign you're doing something wrong. Where hairdressers actually look for a chair, why reply speed beats advert wording, and what a chair needs to offer beyond pay.

item.title: Hybrid pay: mixing rent, commission and salary without the maths falling apart
item.description: Most salons don't run one pay model, they run three at once — rent for one chair, commission for another, salary for the front desk. Here's what has to be true for that mix to add up cleanly.

item.title: Chair rental vs employed stylists: what UK salon owners are weighing up in 2026
item.description: Employed stylists give an owner control over pricing, standards and the client relationship. Chair rental gives that control to the stylist and predictable rent to the owner. A plain look at what each model actually trades away.

item.title: Back bar vs retail: keeping salon stock numbers honest
item.description: Product used on a client and product sold to take home need different counting, not one combined stock number. How to count each so the number actually means something.

item.title: How to reduce no-shows in a UK salon without annoying your clients
item.description: Deposits and reminders both cut no-shows, but neither is free of cost. A plain look at the trade-offs, the difference between a no-show and a late cancellation, and why timing beats wording.

item.title: Double-booked again? Why salon diaries clash and how to stop it
item.description: Double-bookings rarely come from a careless receptionist. They come from two systems each holding a different copy of the same diary. Here's where that gap actually opens, and what closes it.

item.title: Screening stylist applicants without spending a week reading CVs
item.description: Applications arrive all week and get read on Sunday night, by which point the best candidates have taken another job. A faster way to screen.

item.title: Why is salon stock always going missing? Back bar control that works
item.description: Most salon stock isn't stolen, it's unrecorded use. Back bar and retail need separate counting rhythms — not one annual stock take that explains nothing.

item.title: 12 questions to ask before switching salon software
item.description: Twelve honest questions to ask any salon software provider before you switch, covering your data, the changeover, per-stylist cost, and how to leave.

item.title: Live commission tracking: why stylists shouldn't wait for payday to see their numbers
item.description: When commission is only visible on payday, every payslip is a possible argument. Live numbers on the real diary remove the argument before it starts.

item.title: How much hair colour is your salon really wasting?
item.description: Overmixed hair colour goes down the plughole with no record it ever existed. Here's why that happens, and what changes once you weigh the bowl.

item.title: Why colour formulas get lost when a stylist leaves
item.description: A client's colour formula usually lives in a stylist's head or a paper card. When that stylist moves on, here is what actually happens to the record.

item.title: Colour cost per gram: the number most salons don't know
item.description: Most salons price colour by the tube and guess the rest. Weighing the bowl to the gram shows what a head of colour actually costs — and where the money goes down the plughole.

item.title: One diary, one till, one client record: what all-in-one salon software actually means
item.description: Most salon software sold as all-in-one is several tools behind one login, each with its own copy of the client. Here is the test that shows the difference.

item.title: Can an AI answer your salon's phone and still book into the real diary?
item.description: How SalonForge's AI Receptionist books straight into the real Daviana diary, and why that stops the double-bookings a bolted-on phone service can't.

item.title: After-hours salon calls: what happens when nobody's on the desk
item.description: The salon phone keeps ringing after closing, on Sundays, and when the desk is already busy. Most of those calls become someone else's booking, not yours.
